title: Read values out of raw bytes
description:
A memory viewer receives a block of raw bytes and has to show the values in it. Write three readers. Each takes the bytes and an offset into them, and reads a little-endian value starting at that offset.

- `readU32(bytes, offset)` reads a 4-byte unsigned integer.
- `readI16(bytes, offset)` reads a 2-byte signed integer.
- `readF32(bytes, offset)` reads a 4-byte `float`.

If the value would run past the end of `bytes`, the reader returns `std::nullopt` instead.

```
bytes: 0c 00 00 00  00 00 80 3f  9c ff
readU32(bytes, 0)  = 12
readF32(bytes, 4)  = 1.0
readI16(bytes, 8)  = -100
readU32(bytes, 8)  = nullopt   (only 2 bytes left)
```

For the float, build the 32-bit pattern first, then turn the pattern into a float with `std::bit_cast` (from `<bit>`) or `std::memcpy`.
hints: Write a helper that checks whether `count` bytes starting at `offset` are inside the block. Be careful: `offset + count > size` can overflow for a huge `offset`; `count > size - offset` (after checking `offset <= size`) cannot.
Little-endian: byte `i` is worth `bytes[offset + i] << (8 * i)`. OR the four shifted bytes together.
For the float, reuse `readU32` to get the bit pattern, then `std::bit_cast<float>(bits)`.
lessonTitle: Reading the Memory Window in Visual Studio
